subject: Post-demo: ClearWave perf handshake + ops plan
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@clearwave.health>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@clearwave.com
Date: 2026-09-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf goals

Thanks for the demo today — nice to see the streaming preview and the cost tradeoffs live. A couple of clarifying items from our side so we can align with procurement and infra: 

- Latency: our product team is targeting p95 end-to-end < 200ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens). For streaming audio-transcription -> summarization flow we need tail latency for first token <= 120ms and steady-state token gap ~25ms.
- Throughput/concurrency: in peak windows we expect 120 concurrent sessions, average 0.8 requests/sec per session (bursty). Peak TPS ~100 rps sustained for ~5min bursts.
- Streaming: we need server-side streaming (chunked tokens) and the ability to attach per-session context cache since many users repeat similar prompts.

Can you confirm whether the continuous batching + cache approach you mentioned can hit these targets on a dedicated pool? Also please include rough cost delta if we require int8 quantized variant vs full fp16 on the same SLOs.

Sam
Lead PM, ClearWave Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clearwave.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf goals

Sam — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps: 

Recap of targets you listed:
- p95 end-to-end < 200ms for <=128 tokens (short prompts)
- First token streaming <= 120ms, steady-state ~25ms per token
- Peak ~100 rps sustained bursts, 120 concurrent sessions

Initial assessment (high level):
- Dedicated GPU pool with continuous batching + KV/prefix cache should meet p95 <200ms for short prompts using a medium-sized variant (Redwood-medium or similar optimized open model) if we tune batch windows aggressively and use cache for repeated prefixes.
- For first-token streaming <=120ms we will need a low-latency serving configuration (smaller batch cutoffs for streaming endpoints) and potentially reserve burst capacity to avoid queueing on spikes.
- Int8 quantization (optimized kernels) usually reduces memory and increases throughput with a modest latency improvement; however it can increase variance on tail latency unless cache/batching is tuned. We'll run a quick lab verification.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) I'll schedule a short lab run next week to baseline: (a) redwood-medium fp16, (b) redwood-medium int8, (c) redwood-small int8. That will give latency p50/p95/p99 and cost qps estimates.
2) Marissa to draft a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones for perf validation and procurement gating (I attached a draft requirements PDF).
3) Karthik to propose a dedicated pool config (GPU type, instance count, autoscale policy) for the requested burst profile.

Can you confirm an available window for a 90min lab session next Tue/Wed? If you want, we can invite two of your infra engineers so we can exercise real session patterns.

—Marcus
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clearwave.health>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf goals

Sam — attaching the MAP + perf requirements PDF (clearwave_perf_requirements.pdf). Highlights in the doc: 
- Validation checklist (stage 1: synthetic load, stage 2: pre-prod with 10% traffic, stage 3: blue/green rollout).
- SLO acceptance gates (p95 <=200ms, first-token <=120ms) and rollback criteria.
- Cost levers we recommend for the validation window: continuous batching with 20ms batching latency (adaptive during bursts), session-aware KV cache for 90% cache hit target on repeated prompts, and a quantization trial (int8) only for non-critical models.

Quick notes on tradeoffs:
- Continuous batching increases throughput and reduces per-token cost but can add a small fixed latency on first token if batch windows are not adjusted for streaming.
- Cache reduces work for repeated prefixes but requires warmup time; recommend a warmup run with representative session traces.
- Quantization typically reduces instance count (lower cost) but might require extra evals to validate output quality for clinical summaries.

Next step: Marcus and Karthik will propose lab times; Lauren I'll need procurement-related timing/ops support for the reserved capacity quote.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Product GTM — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@clearwave.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf goals

Looping in a proposed config and quick numbers (rough estimates pre-lab):

Assumptions: average prompt 80 tokens, steady-state token generation 15 tokens/sec per session during summarization bursts.

Proposed dedicated pool (starting point):
- GPU type: 4x A100-40GB instances (or similar Ampere cards) in a pooled autoscale group.
- Baseline instance count: 6 GPUs (hand-off to dedicated pool).
- Autoscale policy: add 2 GPUs per sustained 60s over 75% utilization, release after 3min idle.

Estimated sustained capacity (medium model, fp16): ~140 rps with continuous batching + KV cache at 80% hit. Int8 variant could boost throughput ~1.6x but expect a 5–10ms variance on p95 without extra tuning.

Cost levers recommended for SLO alignment:
- Continuous batching: tune batch window per endpoint; streaming endpoints use 10–20ms micro-windows to balance first-token latency vs batch efficiency.
- Prefix/KV cache: prioritize session-level caching for common prefixes — aim for 70–90% hit during peak.
- Quantization profile: run int8 trial on non-critical model first; if quality metrics are acceptable, roll to production for cost savings.
- Model variants: use small/medium tier for interactive flows and large for offline batch summarization. Auto-fallback policy can route to cheaper variant when latency headroom exists.

I'll prepare lab config and cost comparison (per-hour and per-100k tokens) for the experiments.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam@clearwave.health>

Subject: Re: Demo recap — perf goals

Thanks — that all looks good. Wed 9/16 at 10:00 PST for the 90min lab works for us; I'll bring two infra folks (Priya and Daniel) and our product lead to validate quality. Couple of asks before the lab: 

1) Can you include an int8 vs fp16 quality comparison (ROUGE/BLEU + a manual clinical-summary check) in the lab run outputs?
2) Please add a small test that simulates session-level cache warmup to confirm time-to-warm and effective hit-rate.
3) We'll need a one-page procurement summary (cost delta for reserved pool vs on-demand during the pilot) for our procurement team — Lauren, tagging you for timing.

If you can share the MAP and the DocuSign link for the MA draft I can pass to procurement.

Sam
Lead PM, ClearWave Health
